newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Sanlam sees no flat tax on fund assets.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Sanlam sees no flat tax on fund assets.

text.p: The South African government is unlikely to opt to change the formula for taxing retirement funds to one based on a fund's total assets, Sanlam managing director Desmond Smith said on Tuesday.
"I personally don't think we are going to see a flat rate of tax on retirement funds," he told reporters at a results presentation.

Last year the goverment introduced a tax on retirement funds' interest and rental income at the rate of 17 percent, leading to a sharp increase in Sanlam's tax bill. This new tax would inevitably impact on bonus payouts, Smith said.
"As a result of this tax we are going to have to reduce the bonus rates that we declare on retirement fund business by something like half a percent."
There has been speculation that the government was considering changing the tax base to one on total assets, although no such change was announced in last week's 1997/98 budget.
